scenario: [LEXP.3.7.3]: "a null receiver or argument yields null" ([LNUL.4.1]), with no fault, for each of the five members. `x` and `w` are `Int?`. Fact 1 has no `x`, so every member's receiver is null: rule `receiver` fires where `t.x.bits(t.lo, t.w)`, `t.x.sign_extend(t.w)`, `t.x.swap_bytes(t.w)`, `t.x.leading_zeros` and `t.x.trailing_zeros` are all null. Fact 2 has an `x` and no `w`: rule `argument` fires where `bits`, `sign_extend` and `swap_bytes` are null. Rules `type_fault` and `computation_fault` log any TypeError or ComputationError and must stay silent. Messages: `receiver 1`, `argument 2`. A builtin that classed the null as a type mismatch, as `bit_count` does, would log `type_fault` and neither line. PATH PINNED: the null arm ahead of the kind test in FN_BITS, FN_SIGN_EXTEND, FN_SWAP_BYTES, FN_LEADING_ZEROS and FN_TRAILING_ZEROS, in libds (`builtins.c`) and Mercury (`ds.eval`).
rules_ds:
schema T scope logical:
    id: Int key
    x: Int? mutable
    lo: Int mutable
    w: Int? mutable

rule receiver:
    T t where t.x.bits(t.lo, t.w) is null and t.x.sign_extend(t.w) is null and t.x.swap_bytes(t.w) is null and t.x.leading_zeros is null and t.x.trailing_zeros is null
->
    log info "receiver {t.id}"

rule argument:
    T t where t.x is not null and t.x.bits(t.lo, t.w) is null and t.x.sign_extend(t.w) is null and t.x.swap_bytes(t.w) is null
->
    log info "argument {t.id}"

rule type_fault:
    TypeError e
->
    log critical "type {e.rule}"

rule computation_fault:
    ComputationError e
->
    log critical "{e.kind} {e.rule}"
